messages:
maria: heads-up  i built a delta-overlay warmstart prototype for large sharded safetensors. aim: reduce p99 stalls during variant rollouts by streaming small delta segments into an ephemeral overlay and swapping pointers per-layer.
jon: TL;DR?
maria: instead of swapping entire checkpoints or blocking while a big quant blob downloads, keep base safetensors on-disk and populate an in-memory overlay with already-decoded/quant segments. publish is an atomic per-layer pointer update. requests never block on full shard fetch.
ash: neat. how do we represent overlays to the loader? any manifest changes?
maria: minimal manifest extension: segments list + gen + compressed flag. example snippet: ```manifest_v0 = {
  "model": "gptx-30b",
  "segments": [
    {"id": "layer_12_ff", "start": 0, "len": 98765, "gen": 7, "format": "safetensors"},
    {"id": "layer_23_attn_kv", "start": 98765, "len": 12345, "gen": 7, "format": "q4_0+gz"}
  ],
  "overlay_hint": "delta",
  "sig": "sha256:deadbeef..."
}
```
jon: how do you keep KV cache coherent when pointer table changes?
maria: each weight-block carries a tiny generation counter. any KV cache entry is tagged with the gen it was built from. on pointer swap we bump the gen for affected blocks. requests check tag+gen before reusing cached KV; mismatch triggers a quick recompute for that request path. low-cost compare-and-bump.
ash: eviction + fallback? what if overlay space is exhausted mid-stream?
maria: loader writes to ephemeral area; if eviction needed we evict least-recently-used overlay segments, falling back to base safetensors segments. publish is atomic so partial overlays never become live. we also support a soft-fallback path that serves base format while background re-stream attempts to rehydrate overlay.
jon: any perf numbers from the spike tests?
maria: small lab run: rolling 50-node canary, switching a 60GB checkpoint with overlay deltas reduced p99 tail stalls by ~30% vs cold hot-swap; total bytes transferred up ~8% due to delta metadata and small-range fetches. CPU overhead for checksums ~3-4%.
qa-bot: test plan: 1) corrupt manifest fuzz (no crash), 2) partial write recovery (must revert), 3) concurrent publish under 2k qps (measure p50/p99), 4) generation-mismatch KV invalidation coverage, 5) eviction stress (overlay thrash). I'll file tests.
deploy-bot: preview deploy for branch delta-overlay-warmstart created. canary group: 10 nodes in eu-west-1.
maria: operational metrics to add: overlay_coverage (bytes served from overlays), overlay_publish_failures, overlay_gen_rolls, fallback_rate. also trace events for publish latency.
jon: we should formalize a compact ABI so debugger/telemetry tooling can map overlay vs base addresses (pointer table introspection).
ash: consider proactively seeding overlays for high-traffic routes using a small ML predictor  predictive warmup. metric overlay_coverage will help tune that.
maria: agree. i'll write an RFC follow-up with the manifest ABI, publish state machine, and test artifacts. thanks :raised_hands:
